chunks: Then they were filled with remorse and saw that they had erred and said: "If our Lord does not forgive us we will surely be lost."

key_terms.سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ: fell into their hands (metaphor for realization or taking hold of the truth/error)

ai.seo_question: What did the people say when they realized their error and sought Allah's mercy?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from stubborn denial to humble supplication, illustrating that true repentance arises from the recognition of one's own deviation. It underscores the necessity of divine mercy (Rahmah) as the ultimate savior for those who have erred, linking their fate directly to Allah's forgiveness rather than their own merit. This moment serves as a critical lesson in the Quranic narrative of the Children of Israel, emphasizing that regret must be accompanied by a plea for pardon to avoid being among the 'losers' (Al-Kasinun).
